title: Beyond the 956: Martha Firestone Ford, longtime Detroit Lions owner, dies at 101
excerpt: Martha Firestone Ford, the Firestone heiress who became principal owner of the Detroit Lions and led the franchise for six seasons, died November 24, 2026, at her home in Grosse Pointe, Michigan. She was 101.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Martha Firestone Ford, the Firestone heiress who became principal owner of the Detroit Lions and guided the NFL franchise for more than six decades, has died at 101.

Ford died Tuesday, November 24, 2026, at her home in Grosse Pointe, Michigan, surrounded by her family, the Detroit Lions announced. No cause of death was given.

Born Martha Parke Firestone on September 16, 1925, in Akron, Ohio, she was the granddaughter of industrialist Harvey S. Firestone, founder of the Firestone Tire and Rubber Company. She graduated from Vassar College in 1946 and married William Clay Ford the following year, a union that joined two of America’s most famous manufacturing families — Firestone and Ford.

In 1963, she and her husband purchased full control of the Detroit Lions. After her husband’s death in 2014, she assumed sole control of the franchise, leading the team to playoff berths in 2014 and 2016. In 2020, she passed the franchise to her daughter, Sheila Ford Hamp, and served as owner and chair emeritus until her death.

During her tenure, she oversaw a major investment in Ford Field in 2017 and helped launch the Detroit Lions Inspire Change social justice initiative in 2019. She was also a longtime trustee of Henry Ford Health and a supporter of many Detroit-area nonprofits, including organizations focused on women and children.

In 2019, she starred in the NFL Films production A Lifetime of Sundays, a documentary about four matriarchs of NFL families. She remained a devoted presence with the team throughout her life, attending games even this season at 101.

Ford is survived by her four children, 14 grandchildren and 17 great-grandchildren.

Sources: The Associated Press; Reuters; Detroit Lions official statement; People.
